blocks.text: Many nations, hundreds of tongues,
thousands of peoples: such was this world.
Though local strife never wholly ended,
an age worthy of the name "peace"
had lasted over a thousand years.
But this contrived "peace"
lasted far too long for humankind.
It was enough to slow civilization
and to dull humanity's evolution as a species.
Anoian year 5099.
The thousand years of calm
at last passed into history.
It marked the dawn of an age
that later historians would call the "Age of Twilight".
The Kingdom of Asroit and the Republic of Baileste:
two powers gone.
This spurred each people they had absorbed to seek freedom,
and woke national feeling in every heart.
Rivalry among peoples made war crueler still.
On a world map once divided among 12 nations,
half of them gone in less than a year.
over 500 names were written in just 4 years,
The storm of war took even remote, tiny Biastok,
showing no mercy.
The king and his line
were murdered by hereditary vassal Uther Luitgard,
and with that,
Biastok's age of turmoil began.
Lordless, the local magnates each declared independence,
until this one small land held 20 warring states.
War without ideals bred only hatred.
The fighting only grew fiercer.
But into chaos-torn Biastok
stepped one hero.
His name was Arthur Luitgard,
the very son of the man behind the chaos,
Uther Luitgard.
With only one companion, Arthur
seized and jailed his father.
Three nations invaded amid the succession chaos;
he crushed them in turn,
and brought them under his own rule.
A young commander who took 3 nations in just 4 months:
neighboring kings felt the threat.
So it was that 13 nations
closed a ring around Arthur Luitgard.
The league of 13 reeled, its food stores burned,
and Arthur Luitgard
broke them one by one in the Forest of Tintagel.
The storm of war swept the continent.
Lords slew vassals, fearing betrayal,
starving peasants sold their own children.
It was truly the end of the world.
Yet even in this hellish world,
some lived on, unbowed.

Small Aquine in southern Racoss, led by its
"Holy Warrior of Aquine" and "Wise Woman of the West",
beat back 11 invasions across 7 years.
But 8 years after the mountain hut meeting,
Marquis Ardi, the wise lord who raised them both,
was poisoned by his uncle, Count Sampour.
Count Sampour
planned to sell Aquine to the great Duchy of Gaste
next door, in return for rank and lands.
But the people of Aquine would not have it.
Loyal Guyenne and the people
named the "Holy Warrior of Aquine" new lord.
The "Holy Warrior of Aquine"
refused at first, but moved by their fervor,
led the fight against Count Sampour.
The rising of the man called "Devil of Aquine"
shook the Duchy of Gaste,
which disowned the whole affair.
Without his backing, Count Sampour fled,
and his coup ended after just one month.
From then on, Aquine, under its two wise rulers,
enjoyed 40 full years of peace.
Many who longed for a peaceful land,
merchants and farmers, moved there,
until it came to be called the "Capital of the West".
A small land, yet one where all could smile
and live in peace...
There lay an ideal world...
Dream of young Eleanor, Wise Woman of the West.

In the south of old Asroit
lay the vast woodland of "Weisswald".
This poor land, of next to no strategic worth,
could not escape the tide of war.
But in the west of Weisswald,
the "Forest of Mutz" alone was spared.
That forest, as vast as a small nation,
was held by the "Forest Kings",
a band of noble thieves.
The leader of those thieves was named Pasca...
At his side there was always a lone warrior.

The isle of Irenia...
Church, all in a complex tangle:
Even this land, ringed by sea, was no exception.
Let us go back before the "blast of light"...
Baileste had ruled its north,
and that republic's fall brought chaos,
but the southern Kingdom of Irenia seemed set
to unite the isle
and end it with relatively little turmoil.
But power struggles in the Kingdom of Irenia,
the people's anger at their rulers,
the backlash of the Bailesteans who held its economy,
nationalists fighting immigrants,
and papists against the Irenian
on this small island nation,
five nations came to war.
The fighting only grew fiercer.
But into chaos-torn Irenia stepped one man.
That man, whom people called Irenius,
took half the island in just 2 years
and founded the first nation ever to reject nobility outright.
History does not record his true name,
but they say he once
went by the name of Orpheus.
And at his side
stood a lone warrior...
And at his side
stood a lone woman...

Two days later, at Saint Barkail's Cathedral in Lenos,
the "Second Cathedral",
Pope Gregorius VIII, 15 cardinals,
and 87 of their guards
fell at the hands of two men.
News of this abominable deed
swept the continent in a flash.
fell at the hands of a man and a woman.
The Pope's son and his friend: their names

The sudden deaths of the Church's leaders
broke up the Papal Army.
Within a month,
It was absorbed by various small states,
and the Papal Army never formed again.
At the same time,
the Holy See's prestige and power fell far.
Their ruin of the old order
paved the way, in the end,
for Sister Tiara of Cassiz
and Brother Luca of Nasti's religious reform
a year later. That cannot be denied.
They were by no means heroes.
Yet in the end they shaped the future most efficiently,
founding the next age.
Not that reform's standard-bearers
and the greatest villains in religious history
were linked by more than a handful on this continent...

In the "Age of Twilight", as hundreds of nations rose and fell,
there were but five women rulers.
Among them,
only one woman founded a nation herself.
Her nation was the Kingdom of Weihnachten,
lying east of Gasnitz, Asroit's old capital:
a small country.

By chance, that same day, in Lenos, seat of the Anoian faith,
a dozen-odd Holy See notables, Pope Gregorius VIII among them,
were attacked at a rite and all killed:
the worst calamity in the Anoian faith's history.
Holy See's authority collapsed,
the once unstoppable Papal Army broke up,
and its forces were absorbed by small states.
A year later, Brother Luca,
at Nasti Monastery, in what was western Baileste,
proposed a new form of the Anoian faith and its creed,
starting a religious reform.
"Divine nature" dwells in each person
from the very moment of birth.
Without any priest's aid,
each believer, by holding to faith,
can nurture that "divine nature"...
He lived out quiet days in a Baileste mountain hermitage.
